doc.title: Iola Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, CT, July 17, 2011

title: First date at Club Alabam and 'Can Dave Brubeck swing'
summary: Iola tells of her first date to a San Francisco club where a woman asked if Dave was colored; talk of critics doubting his swing and his different style.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: No, I was not. I knew nothing. I knew nothing about it. However, we were talking last night about an incident when we were with some friends. And they asked about when we were first going together and dating. And Dave said on this first major date we had we went to San Francisco and we went to a club that was in the black district of San Francisco, it was called Club Alabam. I was the only white girl in the club. And he knew the musicians who were on the bandstand and they invited him to sit in, which he did, and everyone was enjoying it and the club had booths on all sides and tables in the middle. And I was sitting in a booth. And two couples were in front and one of the women looked over the booth wall and said to me, “Is that boy colored?” And I said, “No I don’t think so.” And she said, “He sure plays like he’s colored.” So that was sort of my introduction into a jazz pianist’s life. Because I had no idea of what it would be like.

Isn’t that funny. You know he sort of had that thing follow him around. I’m sure it’s well gone now, but people talking about, “Can Dave Brubeck swing,” you know, that kind of © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

thing. And I have to chuckle because I have a DownBeat here from 1957, and he responded to that question. He said something like any jackass can swing and I can too. It sounded like it got his dander up a little bit.

Yes, I think because his style was different from the prevailing style of that time, it took some people a long time to kind of accept that it could be legitimate, even if it was different. And it seems to me that in the history of jazz the people who have made some kind of mark, they were different. They introduced something different.
As opposed to just being a craftsman and sort of an innovator.
